doc.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau and Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1957-09-01

title: The 1955 Boston trip, Tony Parenti and praise for George Lewis
summary: They recall Parenti replacing George on the Boston trip in 1955, and Marrero calls George Lewis the greatest player and a generous man, then the tape ends.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Yeah, 1955. In Boston. That's the time George didn't make it up there, did he? No, we had, how do you call it, Perrano. And what? Tony Perrano. Tony Perrano, yeah. Then George got seconded in the yard.

That's a good player too, Bill. Tony can play. But I don't know, I don't know, that's something that George Lewis, that guy can play some kind of it, I swear. I can't find nobody to match it. Man, George, George is, it's that you don't know, but George is the greatest. I think, I put George with any of them, I'm trying to put him with any of them.
